{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/sh

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./ideal_fire.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   -N 1          -> -N 1
#   -n 1          -> -n 1
#   -t 00:10:00   -> -t 10m
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -t 10m --wrap "sh $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: Slurm -J ideal_fire not translated.
  # Performance/ops implication: job identification may be less convenient; runtime performance is unaffected.

  # NOTE: Slurm -o/-e used %j expansion (jobid) which Flux does not provide portably.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: log filenames may not be unique unless you add uniqueness.

  ulimit -c 0
  ulimit -s unlimited
  set -e

  hostname

  . ~rodierq/DEV_57/MNH-PHYEX070-b95d84d7/conf/profile_mesonh-LXifort-R8I4-MNH-V5-6-2-ECRAD140-MPIAUTO-O2

  export MPIRUN="Mpirun -np 1"

  set -x
  set -e

  ls -lrt

  rm -f FIRE_LES.??? FIRE_PGD.???
  flux run -n 1 sh -lc "time ${MPIRUN} PREP_IDEAL_CASE${XYZ}"
  mv OUTPUT_LISTING1 OUTPUT_LISTING1_ideal

  touch FIRE_PGD.des
  ls -lrt

  rm -f file_for_xtransfer pipe_name

  ls -lrt

  # NOTE: Original script submits another Slurm job: `sbatch run_mesonh`.
  # Flux does not run `sbatch`. Omitted.
  # Performance implication: the downstream job will not be scheduled/executed; overall workflow throughput/behavior changes.

  # NOTE: Trailing `ja` in original script has no known meaning; left out.
fi
"
}
